newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian May retail sales up 4.1 pct m/m, 8.9 y/y.
newsitem.headline: Croatian May retail sales up 4.1 pct m/m, 8.9 y/y.

text.p: Croatian retail sales rose 4.1 percent in May from April, while growing 8.9 percent from the same month a year ago, the State Statistics Bureau reported on Tuesday.

January-May retail sales were 8.8 percent higher than in the same period of 1996, it said. All figures represent sales in current prices. May retail price inflation was 0.4 percent and 2.8 percent year-on-year.
May stocks rose 1.1 percent on a monthly level and 12.0 percent from May last year.
Sales of cars, motorcycles and spare parts recorded the highest May rise of 12.8 percent. Household and hardware had the biggest drop of 7.5 percent from April.
Some 500 leading retailers, representing more than a half of the total domestic trade sector, forecast a 2.9 percent rise of retail sales in June.
May gross sales were only 0.7 percent higher than in April, but rose 11.1 percent year-on-year. They were expected to grow 4.9 percent in June. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
